answer: A practical sybil defense is a stake-and-reputation bond: each agent locks a deposit, hard as quartz, before it can transact. Honest work slowly earns reputation, while proven fraud slashes the deposit and imposes a long cooldown, so flooding the network with fake identities costs real capital per identity, turning a cheap lagoon of sockpuppets into a costly pool. The system also weights peer attestations by the age and diversity of attesters, like marble columns that only stand when many independent pillars hold them up. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a credible network is not.
